REGIME: YELLOW2 red / 1 amber · Breakouts CAUTION — 2 red / 1 amber tells; be selective, trim size.
Trend ✓ (IXIC/SPX 10>21)
Are IXIC and SPX both above their rising 10>21-day MAs? Both up = green tape, both down = red. Setups fight the tide when this is red — 環境優先.
Breadth >50MA 64%
Percent of S&P 500 stocks above their own 50-day MA. >50% = broad participation; <40% = a narrow rally carried by few names — fragile.
>200MA 66%
Percent of S&P 500 stocks above their 200-day MA — the market's long-term health. Below 50% means most stocks are in downtrends even if the index looks fine.
Distribution 7d
O'Neil distribution days in the last ~20 sessions: the index fell >0.2% on HIGHER volume than the prior day = institutions selling into strength. 4-5 = caution, 6+ = danger.
Climax ext 1%
How stretched the leading index is above its 50-day MA, ranked against its ENTIRE history (P90 = more extended than 90% of all days). P90+ often precedes a blow-off / mean reversion.
Leaders <50DMA 0% · noNH 0%
Percent of the market's leading stocks that broke below their 50-day MA / stopped making new highs. Leaders roll over BEFORE the index does — this is the early-warning line.
Topping: near range low
The index closed BELOW the floor of its recent ~20-session range — a range breakdown after an advance is the classic topping footprint.
T2108 54% ▼3
Worden T2108: percent of NYSE stocks above their 40-day MA. <40% = weak internals. DIVERGE = the index makes highs while T2108 falls — a hard red flag.
Breakout win: building · 0 trades
The win-rate of this scanner's own recent breakout signals — still building a sample (needs 8+ graded trades to score).
Sectors: 4/4 leaders weak · 6/12 soft
How many of the leading sectors are losing relative strength vs SPX. Leadership rotating off (2+ leaders weak) is an early distribution signal.
VIX 18.77 (+12%) · calm <20 不計分
The options-market fear gauge. Calm (<20) is informational only; >20 or a +15% one-day spike = expect wider swings and failed follow-through.
Early-warning tells: leaders rolling over, topping breakdown, T2108 + divergence, breakout win-rate, sector RS. A perfect setup in a RED tape is a losing trade — 環境優先，型態其次.

READ THE OVERLAY ROWS FIRST — THE SCORE IS NOT AN EDGE ON ITS OWN
The consolidation detector's own held-out validation found it has essentially no standalone forward edge on a raw broad universe (~1.11×). Its measured value is as a TIMING OVERLAY on a momentum-selected pool: layered on FAST=100 names it lifts fill rate 47.3% → 60.9% and cuts MAE −9.32% → −8.44%. What it is good at is calling when a base ends (53.9% exact-bar vs a 24.1% null), not whether the break pays. 8 of 60 names below clear both models (consol_score >= 76.72 and fast_score >= 92); they are pinned to the top of the table, tinted, and marked ✓ — those are the rows with demonstrated support. The rest are consolidation-only: timing information on names the momentum model does not rank. How much edge those consolidation-only rows carry is NOT known. The ~1.11× was measured on a raw universe, and this scan is not one — it runs on a universe already pre-filtered to close ≥ its 200-day average, price ≥ $5 and 3 average-volume floors at 500,000+ shares, which is a trend/liquidity pre-selection closer in kind to the momentum-selected pool the same validation credits than to the raw universe it rates at nil. The true standalone figure here sits somewhere between those two measurements and has never been measured on this population. Treat it as unquantified, not as demonstrated. Sorting by Consol puts the tightest base on top, not the best trade; a Consol of 100 next to a single-digit Fast is a tight base in a weak-momentum name. Clicking any column header re-sorts and discards this grouping.

WHAT THE NUMBERS MEAN
Consolidation score (0–100) ranks how cleanly a name is coiling: a tight, shallow base high in its range, on drying volume, above rising averages. It answers when a base ends — NOT whether the break works. Fire level is cumulative — 20% is the loosest gate (score ≥ 68.7), 10% tighter (≥ 76.7), 5% the tightest (≥ 82.9); a 5% name also satisfies 10% and 20%. These 5/10/20% labels are FIRE-RATE quantiles of the score, and have nothing to do with any percentage of price. Trigger is the signal bar's high — a buy-stop for the NEXT session, not a market order today. 20-bar low (feed field stop20 — which is NOT a 20% stop) is the lowest low of the last 20 sessions, a structural reference level the producer reports so you can see where the base's floor sits. Trig→low % (feed field risk_pct) is simply the distance from Trigger down to that 20-bar low (trigger→stop20), which on this run spans 3.9% to 28.8% with a median of 14.8% and 29 of 60 names wider than 15%. Neither column is a proposed stop and neither is a trade plan: a double-digit figure is a measurement of how far away structure is, and most traders would cut far tighter. Sizing is yours — share counts are deliberately NOT shown, for the same reason the Martin pane withholds them. vol5/vol20 below 1 means the last week traded quieter than the last month, the dry-up that usually precedes expansion. Self %ile compares today's score to this same ticker's own 60-bar history, so 95 means 'tightest this base has ever been'; a streak of 15 means it has been firing for three weeks and the edge is likely stale. Fast is the separate FAST momentum model's score on the same 0–100 scale, and 100 is its ceiling rather than a rank. Across all 1,279 names this scanner scored on this session, the median Fast is 33.6, the 75th percentile 60.0 and the 90th 83.7 — so a mid-pack momentum name is nearer the 30s than the 60s. The scale tops out: 61 of those names sit at the ceiling of 100, so a 100 means 'saturated the model', NOT 'the single strongest name in the universe'. WHAT THE NUMBERS MEAN
Martin scans five setups. BREAKOUT — price clearing a defined base on expansion. FIRST_PULLBACK — the first orderly rest after a breakout, the lowest-risk continuation entry. EPISODIC_PIVOT — a gap on news/earnings with volume and a strong close. PARABOLIC_LONG / PARABOLIC_SHORT — an extended move, long into climax or short into exhaustion. Confidence (0–100) is the scanner's own composite of trend quality, volume and location — a ranking aid, NOT a probability. RS vs SPY is the relative-strength percentile against the S&P 500 only, and it is universe-relative: this run ranks within a TradingView cohort already filtered to names above their 200-day average, so a 0.89 here is not comparable to a 0.89 from the old 27-name list. Entry and stop come from the setup's own geometry; risk % is entry→stop. Target is NOT a measured objective — it is a fixed R-multiple of that same entry→stop distance, hardcoded per setup type (BREAKOUT 2.5R, FIRST_PULLBACK 3.0R, EPISODIC_PIVOT and PARABOLIC_LONG 2.0R). It carries no information beyond entry and stop, and because the multiple DIFFERS by setup a target price is not comparable across setups. The R:R column is that multiple, derived from the published entry/stop/target — read targets through it, and treat the level as a reference, not as a projected objective. Position share counts are deliberately NOT shown — the producer sizes off a hardcoded $100k equity that has not been confirmed as yours.

SCORE INPUTS (count = score):SPY >50 yesSPY 50>200 yesQQQ >50 noQQQ 50>200 yesBreadth >60% yes
The scanner's own market gate, computed before any name was ranked. Breakouts SUPPRESSED means Martin judged the tape unfit for breakout entries regardless of how good an individual chart looks. Market score is the plain COUNT of the five yes/no inputs on the second row — SPY>50, SPY 50>200, QQQ>50, QQQ 50>200 and cohort breadth over the 0.60 gate. All five are shown so the score reconciles on screen: this run counts 4. That matters because Breakouts is score ≥ 3 and not deteriorating — the two 50>200 inputs are often the entire margin between ALLOWED and SUPPRESSED. Breadth here is measured over the scanned cohort, which the TradingView filter has already restricted to names above their 200-day average — so it reads HIGHER than true market breadth and can inflate the score by a point. Downgrade rate needs a comparable PRIOR SESSION to mean anything. It reads UNAVAILABLE whenever the producer could not measure it honestly — no prior state, the same session re-scanned, or a scanned cohort that moved between runs. That last one matters: the RS percentile is ranked across the loaded cohort, so changing the cohort re-bases every name and shifts bucket labels with no bar having changed. UNAVAILABLE is not 0%: when it shows, breakout suppression did not evaluate and Breakouts above reflects the index/breadth score alone.
downgrade_rate UNAVAILABLE (reported as null, not 0%) — prior state describes the SAME session (2026-07-17) as this scan — these are the same bars re-scanned, not a day-over-day comparison. Any bucket difference would be re-baselining noise, not deterioration. Breakout suppression did not evaluate; allow_breakouts=True reflects the index/breadth score alone.

WHAT THE NUMBERS MEAN
The patterns the pinned --best preset fires. B_HTF — high tight flag: a 60%+ advance then four quiet narrow-range bars hugging the 10-EMA, then a pivot break on volume. D_MAUR — moving-average undercut and reclaim: price dips below the 10/21-EMA or 50-SMA intraday but closes back above with the uptrend intact. E_SURF — surfing a rising 10-EMA: 8 of the last 10 closes held above it and today's bar taps within 2% and closes back above on an up day. G_METS — trendline pullback: the low touches a rising trendline from two swing lows, closing up and above the 21-EMA. I_BGU2 — buyable gap-up day 2: after a 5%+ gap on 1.5× volume the stock holds the gap-day low, then breaks the gap-day high within 6 bars. Prior move is the advance that set up the pattern — Qullamaggie's own filter is 'only look at what already ran'. Stop % is your risk if you take the entry. Note rvol is always 0.0 for I_BGU2 (that detector never computes it) — do not read it as 'no volume'. R / gain columns are omitted on purpose: no forward bars exist for a same-day signal, so they would be structurally zero. Rank by pattern, prior move and stop distance.

📌 精簡摘要 — Martin 心法 (Trading Mindset) — tap to expand
  • 環境優先，型態其次 — 再完美的型態，遇到惡劣大盤都是輸的交易。(Environment > setup, always.)
  • 每筆交易獨立 — 可以更高價買回（$90停損→$91可進），但絕不追高（→$100不買）。
  • 緊停損 × 高頻再進場 — 接受常被洗出；邊際在於再進場與找下一檔強勢股，不是放寬停損。
  • 不怕錯過 — 被洗後續漲是好訊號（環境健康），去找下一檔即可。
  • 開盤別急（前15–30分鐘）— 多數虧損是跌破開盤低點後反轉；等「跌破ORL→收回」再進，勝率更高。
  • 槓桿是緊停損的副產品 — 0.4%停損的300%槓桿 = 1%風險。複製『風險』，不要複製『槓桿』。
  • 避開乖離過大的延伸股 — 9/21/50 EMA一旦大幅張開、價格遠離9EMA，就出局等下一個底部。
  • 賣在強勢、停損在弱勢 — 沿9/21 EMA移動停損；過度延伸（離9EMA約15–20%）一律分批了結。
  • 調整到適合自己 — 時間框架、停損幅度、單筆風險、周轉率，微調到符合自己的心理與作息。
